title: Camp Snap Pro Impressions
summary: I went for a test run with the Camp Snap Pro
content:
It's been just over a year since I got an original Camp Snap and I had been eyeballing a Camp Snap Pro but at £100 it was a bit more than I was willing to spend on a novelty camera. Then I was hit with some luck and someone was selling one for £30 brand new on Vinted[1] and I couldn't resist.

It's worth noting that the Camp Snap 2 came out after the Pro and based on some reviews I read, the 2 might be the "better" choice for a lot of people — it's smaller and it can have 6 filters, although it has the 8MP sensor from the original.

Despite how it looks with all the silver, it's very light — it's a fully plastic outer shell just like the standard one. The Pro has a couple of advantages over the original model: a filter toggle to switch between four filters, a 16MP sensor, and a xenon flash. The flash toggle on the front has three modes: on, selfie mode, or off.

The photos themselves are noticeably better, almost at a point where the vintage nature of the camera is lost. I think any further improvements would turn this into a crappy digital camera rather than the fun kind it is now.

The thing I was most interested in on the Pro is the filter toggle. The original model could only handle one filter at a time so switching required connecting it to a computer and installing a new filter. The Pro comes with four pre-installed: Standard, Vintage 1, Vintage 2, and Black and White. I took the same image with all four filters so I could compare them. Vintage 1 is the only one I'm not a fan of but thankfully there's a whole bunch of third-party filters you can install so I'll be replacing that one. This website has some great filters.

  1. The Camp Snap I bought I also got for a bargain on Vinted. I've been very lucky both times. ⤾
